chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Washing the head with the hibiscus (khittim) every Friday is a safety from leprosy and insanity.

key_terms.الْخِطْمِيِّ: Hibiscus (a plant used for ritual washing)

ai.seo_question: What is the benefit of washing the head with khittim on Friday according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) in *Al-Kafi* links the physical act of washing the head with *khittim* (a type of hibiscus) on Fridays to protection from *al-baras* (leprosy or skin disease) and *al-junun* (insanity or loss of reason). In Shia tradition, this practice is viewed not merely as hygiene but as a means of spiritual purification and physical well-being, aligning with the Friday's status as a day of communal gathering and spiritual renewal. The specific mention of 'insanity' underscores the holistic view of health in Imami thought, where physical ailments are often connected to spiritual states.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Washing the head with the hibiscus during every Friday is a safety from the leprosy and the insanity’.
en.sarwar: 10. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Washing one’s head with marshmallow every Friday is protection against leprosy and insanity.’” (The following chapters are best explained by fatwa.)
